statusDetail: Atomic audit of seven representative public routes. Authenticated member-only areas, real account creation, payments, messaging, media galleries and destructive account actions were not covered because no credentials or permission to create data were supplied.

page.notes: A small mobile-specific public site. Core content is server rendered. Authenticated application templates were outside the unauthenticated scope.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT (not mandatory): a screenshot or computed background under an emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark condition will reveal whether surfaces re-tint; the page CSS / a color-scheme declaration is corroborating evidence. The model chooses the method.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is byte-identical in appearance to the light capture, and the platform probe reports colorScheme "normal" with no prefers-color-scheme rule.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: a transition video, or an in-page probe of getAnimations()/computed animation under an emulated prefers-reduced-motion: reduce condition, can show whether motion stops. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: DOM/platform probes report zero active animations on home and registration under reduced-motion emulation, so no motion persists against the preference.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: a screenshot under emulated prefers-contrast: more / forced-colors, or an axe/contrast probe, can show whether controls and text survive. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The forced-colors registration capture preserves visible text, controls, links and focus affordances; Lighthouse contrast audits did not report a failing node.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: a transition video of a route/state change shows whether it animates; the page source / ::view-transition usage corroborates. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: DOM and platform probes show ordinary multi-page links, zero active animations, and no view-transition CSS or meta opt-in.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: source/CSS inspection for animation-timeline: scroll()/view(); a long-task / scroll-handler probe can flag the main-thread anti-pattern. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: CSS inspection found no scroll-linked JavaScript or animation timeline; trace recorded zero long tasks, so native scrolling is not replaced by a main-thread anti-pattern.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: CSS inspection for scroll-snap / overscroll-behavior / physics-based easing vs custom pointermove listeners. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No carousel, draggable item, swipe action or other gesture-controlled surface exists on the audited public templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No carousel, draggable item, swipe action or other gesture-controlled surface exists on the audited public templates.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: a transition video of scrolling, or CSS inspection for scroll-state container queries. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The mobile terms screenshot shows dense continuous content while DOM/CSS inspection found no sticky section navigation, progress indicator, or scroll-state query.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: CSS inspection for anchor-name / position-anchor / position-try on overlays; a screenshot of an open overlay near a viewport edge can show drift. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No tooltip, menu, popover or other anchored overlay exists on the audited public templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip, menu, popover or other anchored overlay exists on the audited public templates.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: CSS inspection for ::highlight / scroll-marker; a transition video can show whether attention is cued after navigation. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Mobile captures show clear primary login/join links and the contact page presents descriptive, task-specific content-removal choices.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: a screenshot on load, or a DOM probe for full-viewport overlays present before interaction. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Screenshots after load show core content immediately with no interstitial, consent wall, autoplay or full-viewport overlay.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: DOM/source inspection for popover / <dialog> / <details> vs custom overlay divs with manual dismiss handling. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No dialog, popover, disclosure or interruptive overlay exists on the audited public templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No dialog, popover, disclosure or interruptive overlay exists on the audited public templates.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: a screenshot plus layout metrics can show the proportion of the viewport given to chrome vs content. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Entry, login and registration captures devote nearly all space to core content and controls with minimal navigation chrome.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: layout metrics (scrollWidth vs innerWidth) and a screenshot at an emulated narrow mobile viewport reveal overflow. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Layout metrics at 390 by 844 report 0 pixels of horizontal overflow on home and registration.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: CSS inspection for @container / container-type; a computed-style probe of the same component in a wide vs narrow container shows whether it adapts. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The same public templates fit both 390 and 1440 pixel captures using fluid logo and form widths, with no clipping or overflow.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: a focus probe (focus an element, read the computed outline) or an axe target-size check; a screenshot of a focused control corroborates. The model chooses.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: screenshot the first viewport and key scrolled states; inspect heading structure, nav labels, button text, and visual hierarchy; a task walkthrough can show whether the next action is obvious. The model chooses.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: run the flow manually with screenshots/DOM snapshots at each step; compare expected vs actual path length; inspect form requirements, navigation continuity, and blockers. The model chooses.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: exercise network delay/failure, invalid input, empty data and success states; screenshot the state messaging and recovery controls; inspect whether browser history and focus remain sensible. The model chooses.

checkOutcomes.reason: This is a sensitive, authenticated adult social service. Exposing account actions to autonomous agents is not an appropriate public-surface requirement without an explicit safety model.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No user-facing summarisation, generation or inference feature exists on the audited public templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No user-facing summarisation, generation or inference feature exists on the audited public templates.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT (not mandatory): compare heap snapshots for retained growth - a baseline, then one taken after repeating the interaction with `--interact` about 10x (the memory-tracer methodology: baseline -> repeat -> post -> compare). Performance.getMetrics (JSHeapUsedSize, Nodes) across the same before/after window is corroboration. If Chrome DevTools MCP is available, follow its memory-leak-debugging skill: capture baseline, target, and final snapshots, then use memlab or the provided comparison workflow rather than reading raw .heapsnapshot files directly. The package-native `heap` primitive remains the default path. This check is only meaningful where the page has a real interaction to repeat; for a static page with none, mark it not-applicable with a rationale rather than fabricating one. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Ten repeated radio/select interactions increased the fresh-profile snapshot by only 14,958 bytes and 174 nodes, with no Detached constructor population.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: a single `heap` summary's totals (nodeCount, totalSelfSizeBytes, constructor population) plus Performance.getMetrics (Nodes, JSHeapUsedSize) give the current footprint to judge against the page's purpose. Chrome DevTools MCP heap snapshots and memlab snapshot analysis can provide the same memory distribution when available. Read summaries or derived analysis, never raw snapshots unless a dedicated heap-analysis tool is doing the analysis. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Registration heap is about 1.72 MB baseline and 1.74 MB post-interaction, proportionate to a small server-rendered form.

checkOutcomes.method: HINT: the `heap` summary by constructor (Detached* nodes) compared across a before/after pair shows a growing detached-DOM population; an `evaluate` probe can sample listener/timer counts (e.g. getEventListeners-style counting, or instrumenting addEventListener/setInterval) before and after the repeated interaction to spot growth. Chrome DevTools MCP heap snapshots plus the memory-leak-debugging skill's common-leak guidance can corroborate detached DOM, listeners, closures, globals, and unbounded caches. Caveat from the memory-tracer and Chrome DevTools MCP guidance: detached nodes can be intentional caches, so judge confidence rather than asserting a bug. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Before/after summaries contain no Detached constructors and repeated controls do not create DOM subtrees; observed growth is small and bounded.

principleOutcomes.reason: The terms explicitly state that the service is English-only, so translation and bidi adaptation are outside current product scope; missing lang is still reported under inclusivity. The audited public templates expose no locale-dependent numeric, currency or interactive date formatting; the only dates are English legal copy. No event scheduling or user-facing time-zone-sensitive date/time surface is present on the audited public templates.

paths.description: Entry and acquisition template: purpose, primary actions, responsive presentation, global network/security/performance and metadata.
Authentication template: labels, autofill, account recovery and document metadata.
Primary registration form: controls, consent, validation, accessibility, forced colors, responsiveness and repeated-interaction memory.
Safety/contact routing template: content-removal choices and owner contact.
Long-form legal content template: headings, legibility, navigation, language/date handling and no-JS delivery.
Sensitive informational content: age-check methods, privacy explanation and heading structure.
HTTP/network failure recovery using a deliberately nonexistent route.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color scheme.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is byte-identical in appearance to the light capture, and the platform probe reports colorScheme "normal" with no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide dark surface, text, link, border and image treatments through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Primary cross-document navigation has no visual continuity.
findings.evidence: DOM and platform probes show ordinary multi-page links, zero active animations, and no view-transition CSS or meta opt-in.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document view transitions for same-origin navigation, with a reduced-motion-safe fallback and restrained shared-element treatment.

findings.summary: The very long terms page provides no position or progress cue.
findings.evidence: The mobile terms screenshot shows dense continuous content while DOM/CSS inspection found no sticky section navigation, progress indicator, or scroll-state query.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a compact table of contents and an accessible scroll-driven progress cue that respects reduced motion.

findings.summary: The viewport policy restricts zoom and several controls have undersized visual targets.
findings.evidence: axe flags maximum-scale=1 as a critical meta-viewport failure on all four templates. The registration probe measures radio buttons and checkboxes at 13 by 13 CSS pixels.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and minimum-scale restrictions, preserve user zoom, and give compact controls and footer links at least a 24 by 24 CSS pixel target with spacing, preferably 44 by 44 for primary touch actions.

findings.summary: Registration errors are delivered as blocking alerts without field-level recovery guidance.
findings.evidence: Calling the page’s own checkForm() on an empty form returned false and raised only “You need to enter a username to use on the site!”; there were no :invalid controls, aria-invalid states, role=alert elements, or live regions.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native constraints and inline field errors after interaction, focus the first invalid field, set aria-invalid and connect messages with aria-describedby or a live error summary.

findings.summary: Image delivery misses basic sizing and responsive-image hygiene despite a very small page.
findings.evidence: The image primitive reports 8 of 8 images without dimensions and no responsive source for the logo. Lighthouse flags unsized and low-resolution images plus short cache opportunities, although the whole page transfers only 22.9 KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width and height, provide a resolution-appropriate srcset for the logo, and retain long immutable caching for static image assets.

findings.summary: Important form controls lack programmatic labels and decorative images are announced as unnamed content.
findings.evidence: axe reports unlabeled username, email, password, all three date selects, and the login persistence checkbox. The home image audit also finds 7 decorative icons without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate visible labels with every input/select, use a fieldset and legend for grouped choices, fix the login checkbox id/for pair, and give decorative icons alt="".

findings.summary: Most public templates lack headings and landmarks.
findings.evidence: axe reports no main landmark across the sampled templates and no H1 on home, login and registration. DOM probes confirm zero main/nav elements and zero headings on the entry page.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce header, main, nav and footer landmarks, add one descriptive H1 per template, and keep a logical heading hierarchy.

findings.summary: Long-form legal content is dense and uses small text with little reading structure.
findings.evidence: The 390-pixel screenshot shows 13-pixel Arial paragraphs spanning nearly the full viewport width; the terms page has one H1 but numbered sections are mostly bold paragraphs rather than navigable headings.
findings.suggestedFix: Use at least 1rem body text, a comfortable line-height and measure, and semantic H2/H3 section headings with a table of contents.

findings.summary: The public templates retain obsolete presentational markup and omit intrinsic image dimensions.
findings.evidence: Rendered HTML uses layout tables, align, hspace and vspace attributes and inline presentational styles; the image inventory reports all eight images without width and height.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace layout tables and obsolete attributes with semantic HTML and CSS, then set intrinsic dimensions on images.

findings.summary: The entry page is not eligible for back-forward cache restoration.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports one bfcache failure reason on the entry page.
findings.suggestedFix: Inspect the Lighthouse bfcache failure reason and remove unload handlers, cache-blocking responses, or other disqualifying behavior where safe for authenticated state.

findings.summary: Public templates have weak or missing search snippets and page titles.
findings.evidence: Login has an empty document title, registration is titled only “register”, and no sampled page provides a meta description. Lighthouse fails the entry page meta-description audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each public template a unique descriptive title and concise meta description aligned with its visible purpose.

findings.summary: The public site provides no XML sitemap.
findings.evidence: The active fetch probe received HTTP 404 for /sitemap.xml. robots.txt exists and intentionally excludes private, login and registration routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap containing only indexable public content and reference it from robots.txt.

findings.summary: Public pages provide no structured data or social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The platform probe finds zero JSON-LD blocks and zero Open Graph metadata on the entry and registration pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite metadata where appropriate and Open Graph/Twitter preview tags for public informational pages.

findings.summary: Security headers are incomplete and sensitive-site cookies are not consistently Secure.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive finds no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Cookie inspection finds AWSALB, AWSALBTG, tc, m and ASP.NET_SessionId without Secure, with several SameSite=None cookies and two 400-day cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, a restrictive CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, choose Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential, and reduce unnecessary lifetimes.

findings.summary: The 404 state is functional but offers almost no recovery help.
findings.evidence: The server correctly returns HTTP 404, but the page contains only “File not found” and one home link, with no search, context, navigation or contact route.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the correct status while rendering the normal shell, helpful copy, primary navigation, search or relevant destinations, and a contact option.

findings.summary: Registration validation is interruptive and not assistive-technology friendly.
findings.evidence: The empty-form test triggers a modal JavaScript alert for the first missing field and exposes no inline invalid state or live announcement.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction or submit using persistent, specific inline messages and an accessible summary instead of alert().

findings.summary: Authentication and registration fields do not consistently expose standard autofill semantics.
findings.evidence: The login username and password have no autocomplete tokens; registration email has none, username disables autocomplete, and the password is DOM type=text despite autocomplete=new-password. “Keep logged in” is preselected.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=username/email/current-password/new-password as appropriate, use type=password for secrets, and make persistent-login consent an explicit informed choice.

findings.summary: All sampled images use legacy formats and omit responsive sizing metadata.
findings.evidence: The image audit reports 8 legacy JPG/PNG/GIF resources, no modern formats, 8 missing dimensions and a missing responsive source for the logo. Total transfer remains an excellent 22.9 KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Where it reduces bytes, serve AVIF/WebP variants and responsive sources, while retaining the site’s strong overall weight budget.

findings.summary: The sign-in surface offers password-only authentication with no passkey option.
findings.evidence: Login DOM contains only username/email, password, persistence and submit controls; there is no WebAuthn or navigator.credentials integration and no permission prompt is made on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys as a phishing-resistant sign-in option, retain password recovery as fallback, and request any device capability only after a clear user action.

taskList.title: Fix form labels, landmarks, headings, zoom and touch targets
Harden security headers and cookie attributes
Replace alert validation with accessible inline recovery
Modernise authentication with passkeys and correct autofill/password semantics
Improve titles, descriptions, sitemap and share metadata
Improve long-form terms navigation and typography
Investigate bfcache eligibility and add restrained page transitions
